24: - `usePluginEvents()` is the inbound, live-only Application Event channel. Subscribe only to names declared in the Plugin manifest and registered through the application's `Agent.appEventSchemas`.
25: - `usePluginService()` remains the component API for named Plugin capabilities.
26: - `/agent-contract/agent-tools.ts` owns the explicit set of frontend capability operations advertised to the Agent.
27: 
28: ## Boundaries
29: 
30: - Do not instantiate an AG-UI client or manage a second Agent Runtime inside a Plugin.
31: - Do not invent a separate public message or state protocol when the Plugin Contract already exposes AG-UI data.
32: - Event, snapshot, delta, streaming, tool-call, and error normalization belongs in the frontend Runtime layer; Plugins render the normalized hook values.
33: - Never expose or import AG-UI `CUSTOM`, `CustomEvent`, `BaseEvent`, `RawEvent`, `rawEvent`, or `@ag-ui/core` from Plugin code. Preserve an explicitly supplied backend business event name and payload; never guess an unknown payload shape. Distinguish its consumers: a chat message renderer uses `defineDataMessageUI`, `definition.dataMessageUIs` and `manifest.data.messageUI`, and validates its raw `data`; a live Application Event subscriber uses `Agent.appEventSchemas`, `manifest.data.events` and `usePluginEvents`. Do not add a duplicate subscriber merely to render a chat message. Application schema transforms do not rewrite message data.
34: - For Application Event subscriptions, reuse an existing schema module; otherwise create an application-owned module relative to actual sourceRoot (for example `agent-contract/agent-events.ts`) and wire it through `Agent.appEventSchemas`. That directory is optional, not a preinstalled Runtime requirement. A Plugin-local schema wired through the application is also valid.
35: - Frontend Tools use standard AG-UI `RunAgentInput.tools`, `TOOL_CALL_*`, `ToolMessage`, and a continuation Run. Never encode a frontend Tool call as `CUSTOM`, a new UserMessage, or a Plugin-specific protocol.
36: - The Agent calls a capability adapter, never React or a Plugin. Reuse or define a stable Service seam, let a Provider Plugin declare and provide that Service, then expose only the product-authorized operations in `/agent-contract/agent-tools.ts`.
37: - Tool names use `lower_snake_case`; schemas use `z.strictObject(...)` as the single validation and JSON Schema source; handlers resolve Services at execution time and return short serializable results.
38: - Do not infer that every Service method should be exposed. Capability ownership and Agent exposure permission are separate decisions.
39: - Plugins must never self-register Frontend Tools or import AG-UI Tool types. They only provide capabilities through the existing Service lifecycle.
40: - Do not invent Application Events to replace standard Activity/Tool/Run lifecycle, persistent shared state, local Plugin communication, or frontend commands. An explicitly supplied business-job CUSTOM notification can drive a live panel through the application channel; it does not become standard Runtime execution progress or gain history/replay. A single Plugin's private projection may use component state and update by the supplied business ID. Subscribe in `useEffect` and return the unsubscribe function. Use existing shared state/services when persistence or cross-Plugin sharing is actually required.
41: - A request for different layout or placement is not an AG-UI Runtime change.
42: - During Phase 8, implement AG-UI presentation inside `/plugins/` while keeping Runtime and Framework source read-only.
43: 
44: For interaction semantics, reason from product needs and AG-UI first. Treat external Agent UI projects as references, not runtime dependencies or public contracts.
45: 
46: ## History, attachments, speech and feedback services
47: 
48: These capabilities have built-in defaults and project-owned service wiring.
49: Business URLs/auth belong in implementation code, not Agent props. Before connecting a business history, upload, transcription or feedback
50: service, read [service configuration](references/service-configuration.md).
51: Users supply endpoint/authentication/payload details. Creator edits wiring and uses the confirmed private implementation change tools
52: for services/ HTTP integration. Explain operation and shared impact before
53: confirmation; public Service contract changes use their separate tools. Report
54: applied changes and verification accurately. Preserve explicit custom adapters and Plugin layout.
55: 
56: ## Frontend Tool execution and replay contract
57: 
58: For capability or renderer integration details, read the packaged
59: [Frontend Tool lifecycle reference](references/frontend-tool-lifecycle.md).
60: 
61: 1. Product side effects belong only in Tool `execute`: open dialog, navigate,
62:    select item, change editor file, modify application state, write storage, copy
63:    clipboard, download, call mutation API, submit form, or trigger a host action.
64: 2. A Tool renderer is a replayable projection. Assume history load, thread/branch
65:    switch, remount, React StrictMode and virtualization can mount it again.
66:    `render / mount useEffect != tool invocation`.
67: 3. Never implement Agent behavior with
68:    `useEffect(() => capability.doSomething(), [])`. Instead use
69:    `execute -> capability.doSomething()` and `render -> args/result/status`.
70:    UI measurement, ResizeObserver, subscription cleanup, focus and animation
71:    effects remain legitimate.
72: 4. Results must carry a historical receipt sufficient to render args/result/status
73:    without checking today's application state. An opened dialog result can contain
74:    `{ opened: true, title: "Settings" }`; history does not require it to stay open.
75: 5. History restoration must never execute Frontend Tools. An execute on history
76:    load is a Runtime bug; do not patch it with renderer `isHistory` workarounds.
77: 6. Keep `Plugin -> Service`, `Application agent-tools -> allowed operation`,
78:    `Runtime adapter -> Agent UI native frontend execute`. Plugins never
79:    register Tools. Preserve root-only execution scope until subagent attribution
80:    has its own contract. Do not add another TOOL_CALL executor or CUSTOM protocol.
81: 
82: ## Official integrations
83: 
84: When Agent UI provides a specialized integration:
85: 
86: 1. Inspect the official integration at the project's pinned upstream revision first.
87: 2. Reuse its public semantic contracts where possible.
88: 3. Do not bypass AgentUICreator application permission.
89: 4. Model reusable adaptation as an Integration, not as a Demo Plugin.
90: 
91: React Hook Form: reuse `@za38.03/agent-ui-plugins/form-tools.formTools` through
92: `integration/react-hook-form`. Use ordinary RHF `useForm()` plus an application
93: Service and `createReactHookFormFrontendTools({ serviceName, fields, expose })`.
94: `expose` is mandatory and has no default. Do not call `useAssistantForm()` or
95: `aui.modelContext.register(...)`; combining those with the factory creates duplicate
96: registration and bypasses application permission.
97: 
98: Integration installation != automatic Agent permission. Only application
99: frontend-tool modules included in the generated allowlist expose operations.
100: Integrations can be pluginless and tool-less. Demo consumers own UI, field names,
101: Service lifecycle and replayable receipts; the Integration owns reusable contracts.
102: 
103: ## Agent UI Generative UI
104: 
105: `@za38.03/agent-ui-plugins/generative-ui` is the canonical component vocabulary and
106: renderer. Prefer official vocabulary before creating custom components. Inspect
107: the project's installed version: do not infer capabilities from unreleased
108: source or from the presence of related CSS selectors.
109: 
110: - Install optional `integration/generative-ui` for the shared factory, official
111:   styled vocabulary, Action Registry and public component export. These files
112:   are managed together as one optional Integration, not a default Foundation.
113: - `createAgentUIGenerativeUI` exposes `present()` and `promptUser()` capabilities.
114:   Capability availability does not grant Agent permission. Do not automatically
115:   mount or advertise `present` / `prompt_user`; explicit Tool authorization requires a separate product decision.
116: - Use the pinned package types and official Form `$input` collection; do not infer availability from CSS selectors.
117: - Keep optional source provenance and official styles under Source Registry;
118:   regenerate from the pinned package-owned upstream source. CSS permits only
119:   mechanical `.agent-ui-conversation` selector scoping, with no visual redesign.
120: 
121: ## Localization ownership
122: 
123: Vendor-owned code must remain locale-agnostic and unmodified; all product
124: localization is owned by AgentUICreator composition, adapters, plugins, and Host
125: UI. Reuse existing official domain copy through `useAgentUILocale(namespace)`;
126: `Agent.locales` overrides only existing keys, not arbitrary new namespaces. For
127: new business copy, reuse or create a project-owned shared messages module with
128: domain namespaces and complete `en-US` / `zh-CN` parity. Select messages there
129: with the unified `useAgentUILocaleCode()` value and pass messages to presentation
130: helpers; do not create per-Plugin i18n hooks, language branches or another locale
131: state. See the packaged Plugin API's localization example. Preserve protocol IDs, enums, schema and persisted fields;
132: locale is a view concern. Prefer public props/composition, then owned adapters.
133: If upstream lacks a seam, record a localization gap instead of modifying vendor.
134: Include `pnpm check:i18n` where available and check new copy during upgrades.

alongside existing Registry, child Slot, Service, and Composition checks:

`validate_creator_changes` already runs `pnpm verify:ui` and `pnpm typecheck`,

Operator inspection protocol in this phase; the Creator completion loop
gets the diagnostics through the existing validation result.
